description: Figure 5(b) is a line chart titled "Loss Ratio w.r.t FLOPs," which plots the ratio of the training loss for various methods to that of the Vanilla model, as a function of the number of floating-point operations (FLOPs). The x-axis, labeled "FLOPs," is on a logarithmic scale, with tick marks at 1e7, 2e7, 5e7, 1e8, 2e8, 5e8, 1e9, 2e9, 5e9, and 1e10. The y-axis, labeled "Loss Ratio (%)," is linear and ranges from 94 to 100. The chart displays eight distinct lines, each representing a different method: Vanilla, StrmLLM(n=64), SepLLM(n=64), SepLLM(n=64, H), SepLLM(n=64, H/T), SepLLM(n=128), SepLLM(n=64, H), and SepLLM(n=128). All methods start with a loss ratio of approximately 100% at the lowest FLOPs. The "Vanilla" line remains relatively flat, staying just below 100%. The "StrmLLM(n=64)" line shows a rapid decrease in loss ratio, reaching about 97% at 5e8 FLOPs and then stabilizing. The "SepLLM(n=64)" line shows a similar trend but with a slightly slower initial decrease. The "SepLLM(n=128)" line starts at 100% and decreases more rapidly than "SepLLM(n=64)," reaching a loss ratio of approximately 96% at 5e8 FLOPs. The "SepLLM(n=64, H)" and "SepLLM(n=64, H/T)" lines follow a similar pattern to "SepLLM(n=64)" but are consistently slightly lower. The "SepLLM(n=128)" line is the lowest, showing the most significant improvement, reaching a loss ratio of about 95% at 5e8 FLOPs and remaining the lowest throughout the rest of the range.
